lines.text: This is Moment.
One moment a day, for the Seeker community, powered by Solana and SKR.
Social apps reward endless scrolling.
Moment rewards something rarer: showing up.
Once a day, you capture what's in front of you, and yourself, in the same instant.
And you put your presence on the line.
Connect your wallet through Mobile Wallet Adapter.
Stake at least five hundred SKR. It stays yours, locked in the program's vault.
Take a photo of the scene, then a selfie.
Review, sign, and publish.
Your Moment unlocks today's community feed, and your streak grows.
Now, the SKR economy. Every UTC day is a round.
Miss one, and ten percent of your remaining stake is deducted.
A thousand SKR becomes nine hundred, then eight hundred and ten.
Keep missing, and it keeps shrinking: after a month, barely four percent is left.
Those penalties fund that day's pool.
At six AM UTC the next morning, it closes, and it's split between everyone who posted, pro rata to their stake.
Stake fifteen hundred out of a three thousand total, and you take half the pool, added straight to your stake.
No tokens are minted to pay rewards, and there's no protocol fee.
Every reward is SKR forfeited by someone who didn't show up.
If nobody posts, the pool rolls over to the next day.
And when you're done, request a withdrawal: forty-eight hours later, your stake comes home.
For SKR, that means real utility:
a daily reason to hold and lock the token, rewards for consistency rather than speculation, and identity through .skr names.

lines.text: Under the hood: a native Kotlin app, built for Seeker.
Your wallet signs a manifest of both photo hashes. Its SHA-256 becomes the on-chain commitment.

lines.text: Photos are stripped of metadata, then encrypted with AES-GCM.

lines.text: An on-device model screens them. Then our Rust keyserver re-checks everything, and cosigns the check-in.
It can authorize a post. It can never move your stake.
On chain, an Anchor program enforces every rule, across four accounts: Config, Profile, Day Pool, and Check-In.
Settlement is permissionless: a crank settles missed days, rolls empty pools forward, and refunds rent from old check-ins.
Moment is running on devnet today: Android app, Anchor program, Rust backend, tests, and CI.

Moment. One moment a day.
